insights.headline: Silver's India shortage is policy-made, not demand-led; weak US jobs data keeps Fed-pause hopes alive
insights.summary: A new analysis pins India's silver import collapse — 534.3 to 46.8 tonnes this May — on licensing curbs and the 15% duty rather than weak demand, with MCX silver 17% above the world price at end-September. The soft US September jobs report lifted gold to $4,210 and cooled October Fed hike bets, though high bond yields remain a drag. RBI data showed forex reserves falling $18.34 billion to $747.56 billion for a third straight week as dollar sales defended the rupee; gold reserves slipped $2.59 billion to $108.7 billion. In India, bullion markets were closed for Gandhi Jayanti; Thursday's...
points: Silver imports fell to 46.8 tonnes in May from 534.3 a year earlier; MCX silver was 17% above world prices on Sep 30.
US added 29,000 jobs in September vs 90,000 expected; gold rose 0.8% to $4,210 and October Fed-hike odds fell to 12-19%.
Forex reserves fell $18.34B to $747.56B for a third straight week; RBI gold reserves down $2.59B to $108.7B.
MCX was shut for Gandhi Jayanti; Thursday's Delhi gold was Rs 1,49,800/10g and silver Rs 2.27 lakh/kg.
With gold at Rs 1.5 lakh/10g, middle-class buyers are shifting to silver; IBJA sees Diwali silver demand up 17-18% YoY.

trending.title: Weak US jobs data revives Fed-pause bets
trending.summary: A 29,000-job September print, far below the 90,000 expected, lifted gold to $4,210 and slashed October hike odds — but surging long-end bond yields are capping the rally.

trending.title: Rs 1.5 lakh gold pushes buyers toward silver
trending.summary: With 10 grams of gold costing Rs 1.5 lakh, middle-class Indian buyers are buying silver instead — festive silver demand is expected to rise 17-18% year-on-year.

trending.title: RBI burns reserves defending the rupee
trending.summary: Forex reserves fell $18.34 billion in a week — the third straight drop — as the RBI sold dollars; the steady drain is the backdrop to India's bullion import curbs.

items.title: Silver's India Problem Was Policy, Not Demand
items.summary: India's silver imports fell to 46.8 tonnes in May from 534.3 tonnes a year earlier after the duty rose to 15% and licence rules tightened, recovering to about 15.5 million ounces in August as permits arrived, per Heraeus. MCX silver stood 17% above the world price on September 30, and demand from jewellery, coins, ETFs and industry stays intact, the analysis says. Silver was collateral damage...

items.title: Soft September jobs report sends markets higher
items.summary: US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, far below the 90,000 economists expected, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2%. Treasury yields fell and the odds of a Fed rate hike at the October meeting dropped to around 12-19%. Gold rose 0.8% to $4,210 on the cooler data.

items.title: Fed's Jefferson urges patience on rates; Kashkari sees more hikes ahead
items.summary: Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said he saw 'no urgency' for another rate move despite backing last month's hike, urging patience as markets reassess rising bond yields. Minneapolis Fed chief Neel Kashkari struck a hawkish note, saying more hikes will probably be needed — one more this year and another in 2027 — warning policy may need to go higher if a resilient economy keeps inflation sticky.

items.title: Entrenched premium leaves gold primed to climb despite surge in US bond yields
items.summary: Gold's resilience above $4,000 as Treasury yields hit their highest since 2002 points to a durable post-2022 demand premium, Reuters analysis says. MKS PAMP's Nicky Shiels estimates the 'debasement and de-dollarisation' premium — the slice not explained by real yields and the dollar — has averaged over $1,000/oz since 2022 and stands near $840 now, driven by central-bank reserve diversification.

items.title: Risks rising that gold prices fall below $4,000 in Q4 - Bank of America
items.summary: Bank of America sees rising risks that gold falls below $4,000 an ounce in Q4, Kitco reports. The bank — among the first to call $5,000 — keeps its bullish 2027 view but expects gold to average $3,750 in Q4 as elevated energy prices sustain inflation fears. Crowded positioning is the biggest near-term risk: if Middle East tensions don't resolve, a rapid unwind could pressure gold lower quickly.

items.title: Gold at Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams is pushing middle-class Indian buyers to silver
items.summary: Indian buyers are shifting from gold to silver this festive season: 10g of 24-karat gold costs about Rs 1.5 lakh — the same money buys roughly 650g of silver, TOI reports. The IBJA estimates Diwali-season silver demand will rise 17-18% year-on-year; silver imports topped $1 billion in August, up 127% on the year. A Surat jeweller says silver now makes up to 35% of yearly revenue, up from 10%.

items.title: MCX Gold Faces Rs 1.5 Lakh Resistance After Yield Spike
items.summary: MCX gold October futures jumped 1.02% to Rs 1,47,649/10g but face a Rs 1.5 lakh resistance after a US Treasury yield spike, NDTV Profit reports, while MCX silver December futures rose 0.94% to Rs 2,25,804/kg. The article lists the key support and resistance levels traders are watching on both metals.

items.title: Gold futures rise to Rs 1.50 lakh/10 gm on firm spot demand
items.summary: Gold futures rose Rs 1,475 to Rs 1,50,511 per 10 grams on MCX on Thursday as speculators created fresh positions on firm spot demand, PTI reported. The October contract traded 0.99% higher in 2,019 lots. Gold futures also rose 0.59% to $4,182.06/oz in New York.

items.title: Silver Prices Fall ₹5,000 Today, Down ₹10,000 This Week
items.summary: Delhi bullion trade saw gold add ₹500 on Thursday to ₹1,49,800 per 10 grams on a weaker rupee — ₹96.31 against the dollar, its softest in over two months — even as silver fell ₹5,000 to ₹2.27 lakh per kg. For the week, gold is down about ₹2,800 and silver about ₹10,000. Bullion markets are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti.

items.title: Gold price today: Precious metal slips ahead of US Jobs data; MCX closed for Gandhi Jayanti
items.summary: MCX is fully closed on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti — gold, silver and all commodities suspended, trading resumes Monday, Oct 5. Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,154.78/oz, set for a second straight weekly loss. LKP Securities' Jateen Trivedi sees gold in Rs 1,48,000–1,52,500 with support at $4,125 and resistance at $4,200 ahead of the US payrolls report; Delhi physical 24K at Rs 14,940/g.

items.title: Gold rises Rs 607 as rate-hold expectations strengthen; silver jumps Rs 2,828
items.summary: Softer-than-expected US inflation strengthened Fed rate-hold expectations and lifted Indian bullion, Business Standard reports: MCX December gold opened Rs 607 higher at Rs 1,49,643/10g and December silver opened Rs 2,828 higher at Rs 2,26,534/kg, with Comex gold trading near $4,200/oz. The article lists key support and resistance levels for both metals.

items.title: India's Forex Reserves Plunge by $18.34 Billion
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $18.34 billion to $747.56 billion in the week ended September 25, RBI data released on Friday showed — the third straight weekly decline, pulling the kitty further from its September 4 record of $785.71 billion. Foreign currency assets dropped $15.57 billion to $615.41 billion as the RBI sold dollars to steady the rupee, while gold reserves fell $2.59...

items.title: Gold gets its festive shine back as lower prices lure Asian buyers
items.summary: Lower gold prices are pulling physical buyers back across Asia ahead of the festive season, the Times of India reports: Indian dealer discounts narrowed from up to $43/oz to $14/oz as demand improved, Singapore dealers saw stronger buying as they rebuilt inventories, and China is watching price moves closely with premiums running high.

items.title: Gold, silver prices edge higher: How festive demand could shape the outlook
items.summary: Gold and silver edged higher on October 1 — MCX December gold at Rs 1.49 lakh/10g, December silver at Rs 2.24 lakh/kg — ahead of India's festive season, CNBC-TV18 reports. Ventura's NS Ramaswamy sees gold caught between high yields and support from central-bank buying and ETF flows; Kama Jewelry's Colin Shah says festive demand stays resilient, though high prices push buyers to lighter jewellery.

items.title: Gold price future roadmap: What led to 6% yellow metal fall in Sept 2026? Will Diwali help bounce back?
items.summary: Analysts say festive and wedding demand could support gold after its ~6% September slide, Mint reports. Brickwork's Rajeev Sharan expects Dussehra-to-Diwali buying to keep demand healthy in value terms, though record prices may push buyers toward lighter jewellery, coins or digital gold. Gold opened October near $4,150; soft August core PCE cut October Fed-hike odds to ~34-38%.

items.title: '50% of silver rally was just bubble': experts pick gold and platinum
items.summary: Four Indian market experts argue about half of silver's early-2026 rally was a speculative bubble — the metal has fallen from a January peak of Rs 3.86 lakh/kg to about Rs 2.22 lakh — and they now favour gold and platinum, Bhaskar English reports. They see silver possibly recovering toward Rs 3-4 lakh/kg by 2027, though small investors may wait until end-2027 to recoup older holdings.

items.title: Silver price forecast: XAG/USD rises to near $61.40 as US yields retreat, NFP eyed
items.summary: XAG/USD rose ~0.55% toward $61.38 as the Treasury yield rally paused, FXStreet reports. Markets await September US nonfarm payrolls at 12:30 GMT (consensus +90,000 jobs, 4.1% unemployment) after the Fed's September hike to 3.75–4.00%. Technically silver trades below its 20-day EMA at $63.48 with RSI near 41.6; resistance at $62.19, support at $60.00.

items.title: Silver Falls 45% From Its 2026 Peak as Sierra Madre Scales Up Production
items.summary: Silver has fallen ~45% from its January 2026 peak near $115/oz to about $63 by mid-September, Carbon Credits reports, as producer Sierra Madre scales up output. The World Silver Survey 2026 put 2025 mine output up 3% at 846.6 Moz, yet total demand of 1.13 Boz left a 40.3-Moz deficit — the fifth straight annual shortfall — with a 46.3-Moz deficit expected in 2026.

items.title: Gold steadies as easing US bond yields reduce rate-hike bets
items.summary: Spot gold held near $4,180/oz on Friday, up ~0.5% on the day, as US bond yields retreated from 24-year highs and Fed Vice Chair Jefferson's call for patience cut October hike odds to ~27% from 70% earlier in the week. Gold is still on track for a ~2% weekly loss ahead of the September payrolls report at 12:30 GMT; a firm dollar caps the rebound. Oil rose on Middle East escalation fears.

items.title: Gold price at $4,158/oz after ISM Manufacturing PMI dips to 54.5, prices shoot higher
items.summary: Gold held near $4,158/oz after the ISM manufacturing PMI slipped to 54.5 in September from 54.6, below the 55 consensus, while the prices-paid component shot higher, Kitco reports. Spot gold touched $4,139 overnight before steadying, as the mixed report kept Fed policy expectations in flux ahead of Friday's payrolls data.

items.title: SGB premature redemption October 2026: 4 tranches eligible for early exit, check RBI dates and deadlines
items.summary: Four SGB tranches are eligible for premature redemption in October 2026: 2019-20 Series V (Oct 15; request by Oct 5), 2020-21 Series VII (Oct 19; by Oct 9), 2020-21 Series I (Oct 28; by Oct 19) and 2019-20 Series VI (Oct 30; by Oct 21). Exit is allowed only after five years on scheduled dates; redemption value is linked to the IBJA's 999-purity gold average over the preceding three working days.
